subject.title: [Feature]: Support plugin-requestable session isolation for trust boundaries

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public Plugin SDK isolation directive for untrusted work, and if so what security guarantees and trust metadata must the runtime enforce?
rationale: The code can implement several shapes, but the durable decision is a product/security contract for plugin authors and users, not a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Design after prerequisites
options.body: Keep this issue open and define the isolation API after the hook-context and persistence-policy prerequisites are settled, reusing current subagent and sandbox primitives where possible.

options.title: Narrow to capability policy first
options.body: Treat this as blocked by a broader capability/permission model and defer plugin-requested isolated execution until tool constraints are enforceable.

options.title: Reject core isolation API for now
options.body: Document that strong trust boundaries require separate gateways or hosts and leave plugin-level trust metadata to external/plugin-only experiments.

recommendation.title: Design after prerequisites
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and define the isolation API after the hook-context and persistence-policy prerequisites are settled, reusing current subagent and sandbox primitives where possible.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the central subagent and plugin hook paths that would need to define the runtime boundary.
